title: Performance Optimization
prompt:
Improve calculation speed and maintainability of a large workbook.

Skills: Formula design, efficient ranges and profiling.

Use the supplied synthetic CSV at assets/data/practical-24-performance-optimization.csv. A small copy/pastable sample is included below in case the CSV is not directly downloadable from the lesson page. Complete the work in a separate .xlsx copy, preserve a raw-data sheet, and check the result against the acceptance criteria. Then answer the short grading check; it does not validate the workbook itself.

Sample CSV (synthetic):
Pattern,Risk,Improvement
Whole-column formula,Unneeded calculation span,Bounded table references
Repeated lookup,Duplicate work,Reuse a helper result or LET where supported
Volatile function,Frequent recalculation,Use a non-volatile alternative if appropriate
objective: Improve calculation speed and maintainability of a large workbook.

options: Measure before and after, change one cause at a time, and confirm the results still match.
Use a shorter formula without measuring its performance.
Optimize first and do not rerun regression checks.

expected_output: Expected: a repeatable before/after timing or complexity comparison is recorded without changing the intended results.

public_tests.name: Sample-data acceptance
checklist: Input records are preserved and data types are checked.
Totals/results reconcile with a small independent calculation.
An edge case, duplicate or threshold boundary is tested where relevant.

public_tests.name: Server-side answer check
public_tests.note: A text/choice check does not execute Excel or inspect the workbook artifact.

acceptance_criteria: Expected: a repeatable before/after timing or complexity comparison is recorded without changing the intended results.
Use a labeled result area and document formulas, assumptions or transformation steps.
Compare actual results with a manual/independently calculated expected result and test one edge case.
Keep source data intact and request human review of the completed workbook; do not treat the text grader as artifact validation.
hints: Import data without losing dates, decimals or leading zeros.
Separate raw inputs, calculations and presentation outputs.
Test empty inputs, duplicated keys, boundary values or missing matches as appropriate to the scenario.

grading_config.correct_answer: Measure before and after, change one cause at a time, and confirm the results still match.

grading_method: Server-side choice check of the submitted answer/expression only; does not execute Excel or inspect the workbook. This workbook-practice task needs a human-reviewed artifact and test evidence for full acceptance. A performance optimization should be measured and regression-tested; a shorter formula is not automatically faster or safer.
retry_policy: Retries are permitted. A failed string/choice submission does not complete the exercise. Course files do not define XP; platform-wide server logic applies.
